name: NocoDB
description: A no-code database: tables edited as a spreadsheet and shown again as forms, kanban boards and galleries, each one also served as a REST API. It keeps everything in its own SQLite file on the data volume.

access.note: NocoDB creates one super-admin account the first time it starts on an empty database: the address you enter here, with the generated password from the Variables tab. Sign in with those, then change the password inside NocoDB — these two values only seed that very first account, so a later redeploy that rotates the password will not reset the account you already have. Public sign-up stays open until you close it: a stranger who finds the address can register, though the account arrives with no access to any base and cannot create one. Close it in NocoDB's super-admin settings, under Account Settings, where invite-only sign-up is a toggle; the NC_INVITE_ONLY_SIGNUP environment variable is no longer read in this version.

inputs.name: domain
inputs.label: Public domain
inputs.description: The address other people open. NocoDB ignores the proxy's forwarded scheme and would otherwise report its own origin as plain http, so it is told this address instead — which is why it is required here.

inputs.name: admin-email
inputs.label: Super admin email
inputs.description: The address that signs in the first time. NocoDB uses it as the account name; it never sends mail to it unless you configure SMTP.

ports.name: http
ports.purpose: The web interface and the REST API

volumes.name: data
volumes.purpose: The SQLite database holding every base, table and view

update.notes: NocoDB runs its own schema migrations on start, and the first start after an upgrade can take several minutes before the address answers.

secrets.name: admin-password
secrets.label: Super admin password
secrets.description: Only used to create the first account; change it inside NocoDB afterwards.
